the same six probabilities, read by each strategy

Greedy reads one number: the largest. Top-k sampling throws away all but the k best, reshapes what is left with the temperature, and draws. Beam search keeps the B best and carries them BOTH forward, to be judged later by the whole sentence.

C · The same three, run to the end of a sentence
the hand-set model of deep dives

Each step multiplies the sentence’s probability by the probability of the token chosen. Greedy maximises each factor as it goes; beam search compares the products of several candidates; sampling does not compare at all — it draws, so it can return many different sentences.

D · How a sentence’s probability is calculated
the chain rule, logs, and the length penalty
sentence would be a product of

small probabilities. Logs turn the product into a sum, which is exact and cheap, and the order is the same. Every log-probability is negative, so a longer sentence has a lower score just for being longer.

svg.text: from one token to a whole sentence

text.tspan: the chain rule: the probability of a sentence is the probability of its first token, times the second given the first, and so on. Nothing in the model computes it — the decoder gives

svg.text: log P = Σ_t log p(y_t | y_<t, x)

: without it beam search would prefer to stop as early as possible.
